faqs.question: I see horizontal or vertical lines in my printout. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Perform a nozzle check from the printer's control panel or the Epson printer driver, then do one of the following:
If there are gaps in the nozzle check pattern, clean the print head nozzles.
If there are no gaps in the nozzle check pattern, try the solutions below.
Horizontal Banding
Increase the print resolution.
Turn off
Simple Settings
and uncheck the
High Speed
setting in the printer driver.
Select an alternate paper profile for ink coverage.
Select the correct paper type in the printer driver.
Adjust the paper feed
Vertical Banding
Turn off
Simple Settings
and uncheck the
High Speed
setting in the printer driver.
Align the print head.

faqs.question: Can I use an expired ink cartridge in my printer?
faqs.answer:
Epson does not recommend using expired ink cartridges in the printer. Do not use an unopened ink cartridge if the date on the package has expired. For best results, use ink cartridges before the expiration date printed on the package (and within six months of installation in the printer). Replace expired cartridges with new ones.
You may need to replace a cartridge that is more than six months old, if your printouts do not look their best, even after cleaning and aligning the printhead. We recommend you store any unused or unopened ink cartridges in a cool, dark place.

faqs.question: The colors on my printouts do not match the colors on my computer monitor. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following recommended color correction methods:
Use ICC profiles during the color management process.
Ensure that you are using the correct output profile for your loaded media.
Note:
You may need to create a custom ICC profile for the best results.
Ensure that your monitor is calibrated and is displaying accurate color.
Compare the print result with the image on your computer screen in a well-lit environment. Since monitors and printers produce colors differently, printed colors and screen colors do not always look the same.
If the recommendations above do not help, contact Epson support.
The color management process is complex. We can assist you with the proper assignment of settings; however, we cannot assist you with creating a custom color profile.

faqs.question: Why do I need color ink cartridges when I print in black only?
faqs.answer:
The printer will not print if any ink cartridge is expended or removed. Epson printers contain a permanent print head that needs to be charged with all colors to work. Even when you are printing black text only, a small amount of color ink is used to keep the print head charged. The print head needs to be kept charged to prevent air bubbles from entering. Air bubbles can damage the print head.
Therefore, once one of the cartridges is expended, the printer signals you to replace the cartridge in order for printing to continue.

faqs.question: I see the message No Ink Cartridge Install Ink Cartridge when all ink cartridges are installed. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The ink cartridge(s) you installed may not be recognized by the printer. Try reseating the ink cartridge(s) and turning the printer off and on. If you still see the error message, try installing a different ink cartridge in the printer.
If this did not solve the problem, contact Epson support.

faqs.question: I can tell some ink is still in the ink cartridge. Why does my printer show that the cartridge is expended?
faqs.answer: The ink cartridge is designed to include a small safety reserve of ink. This safety reserve prevents damage to the printhead. If the printer tries to print when no ink remains in the cartridge, air bubbles would enter the ink delivery system and cause damage to the permanent printhead. The safety reserve of ink prevents this from happening.

faqs.question: I see the message Ink Cartridge Error: Replace Ink Cartridge. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
An ink cartridge in your printer needs to be replaced. The cartridge may be expended, or the IC chip on the cartridge may not be communicating properly. Try reseating the cartridge and turning the printer off and on. If you still see the error message, try installing a different ink cartridge in the printer.
If this did not solve the problem, contact Epson support.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.

faqs.question: I see the message Communication Error when I use a USB connection. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Delete all print jobs in the print queue.
Turn the printer off.
Note:
Make sure the USB cable is connected correctly.
Restart your computer. When the desktop appears, turn your printer on and follow the on-screen instructions.
Note:
If the problem continues, turn the printer off again and delete the printer in the list of printers. Then disconnect the USB cable from the printer and connect it again.

faqs.question: What size ink cartridges are included with my product?
faqs.answer:
The ink cartridges contain 110 ml of ink. The cartridges shipped with your printer are provided mainly to charge the ink system. Make sure you order a new set of cartridges as soon as possible.
Related references
Ink Cartridge and Maintenance Box Part Numbers

faqs.question: Does my product have a pressurized ink delivery system?
faqs.answer: Yes. The pressurized system ensures ink flow even when the printer is used at higher elevations or if the floor beneath the printer is not absolutely level.

faqs.question: How many ink cartridges does my product use?
faqs.answer:
See below for your printer.
SureColor P6000, SureColor P8000
The printer has nine ink cartridges, but it uses only eight cartridges at a time to print. The printer switches between Matte Black (MK) ink and Photo Black (PK) ink automatically, depending on the type of media you load.
SureColor P7000, SureColor P9000
The printer has eleven ink cartridges, but it uses only ten cartridges at a time to print. The printer switches between Matte Black (MK) ink and Photo Black (PK) ink automatically, depending on the type of media you load.
Also, your printer uses either Light Light Black (LLK) ink or Violet (V) ink, depending on the edition you purchased. You cannot switch between these inks once the printer is initialized.
Note:
To disable automatic black ink switching, press the
Menu
button, then select
Printer Setup
>
Auto Black Ink Change
>
Off
.
Related concepts

faqs.question: What is the smallest drop size my product will produce?
faqs.answer: The smallest drop is 3.5 picoliters.

faqs.question: Can I change my product's ink configuration from the Standard Edition to the Commercial Edition or vice versa?
faqs.answer: No. The printer is available in either the Standard Edition (Light Light Black) or Commercial Edition (Violet). The ink configuration is permanent once the printer completes its initial ink charge and cannot be changed.

faqs.question: Do I need to drain the ink cartridges before transporting my product?
faqs.answer:
No, do not drain the ink cartridges, and do not remove the cartridges from the printer. The printer has ink valves to prevent spilling ink during transportation.
Related information
Moving or Transporting the Product

faqs.question: Are the ink cartridges compatible with other Epson P-Series products?
faqs.answer:
Yes, the ink cartridges can be used with the Epson SureColor P6000, SureColor P7000, SureColor P8000, or SureColor P9000. However, the Orange (OR) and Green (GR) ink cartridges can be used with the SureColor P7000 and SureColor P9000 only.
Also, only the Commercial Editions of the Epson SureColor P7000 and SureColor P9000 can use Violet (V) ink cartridges. The Commercial Edition uses a Violet (V) ink cartridge in place of the Light Light Black (LLK) ink cartridge.

faqs.question: When should I switch the black ink type to Matte Black?
faqs.answer:
You should switch when printing on non-glossy paper, such as Epson Presentation Paper Matte or Epson Velvet Fine Art Paper. Matte Black (MK) ink produces better black ink density on these paper types than Photo Black (PK) ink. See the link below for a list of Matte Black ink and Photo Black ink media types.
You need to switch the black ink type only if you disabled automatic black ink switching. Because this process consumes some ink, you should avoid switching black ink more often than necessary and select a default black ink type for the type of media you print on most often.
Note:
To disable or enable automatic black ink switching, press the
Menu
button and select
Printer Setup
>
Auto Black Ink Change
, then select
Off
or
On
.

Black Ink Type Media List

faqs.question: Which print head alignment options are recommended?
faqs.answer:
Epson recommends selecting these print head alignment options in the following order:
Uni-D
- aligns each color for uni-directional printing based on Light Cyan.
Bi-D All Color
- aligns each color for bi-directional printing based on all colors.
Note:
Align the print head only if you're experiencing print quality issues and cleaning the print head did not resolve the issue.

faqs.question: Which paper core sizes can be used with my product?
faqs.answer: The printer supports 2-inch (51 mm) and 3-inch (76 mm) paper cores.

faqs.question: Which interfaces does my product support?
faqs.answer:
Hi-Speed USB (compatible with the USB 2.0 specification) and 10BASE-T/100BASE-TX/1000Base-T are supported.
Note:
Use a category 5 or better shielded twisted pair cable.

faqs.question: Does my product come with an Epson printer driver?
faqs.answer: Yes, a print driver is available. You can download the driver from the Downloads tab for your product.

faqs.question: What does the High Speed setting in the Epson print driver do?
faqs.answer: When the High Speed setting is selected, the print head prints in both directions (bi-directional) to speed up printing. This may reduce print quality.

faqs.question: Does Epson offer RIP software for my product?
faqs.answer: No, Epson does not supply RIP software for the printer. RIP software is available from third-party vendors.

faqs.question: Do I need to use RIP software with the Commercial Edition of my product?
faqs.answer: It is recommended that you use RIP software with the Commercial Edition. However, Epson also provides a print driver for the printer. You can download the print driver from the Downloads tab for your product.

faqs.question: What is the Epson Remote Panel 2 Utility?
faqs.answer:
The Epson Remote Panel 2 Utility can be used to do the following:
Adjust the paper feed
Create custom paper settings
Perform bi-directional and uni-directional alignments
Perform nozzle checks
Perform power cleanings
Print status sheets
Set the printer's clock
See Downloads to download the utility.

faqs.question: How do I get service for my product I purchased in another country?
faqs.answer: Due to differences in products sold in other countries, the printer needs to be serviced in the country of origin.

faqs.question: Which connection type enables my product to operate at full speed?
faqs.answer:
Both USB and Ethernet connections enable the printer to operate at full speed. Your CPU affects the printer's speed most. Your CPU should be a Core 2 Duo 3.05 GHz or better.

faqs.question: What is the Roll Media Length Tracking system?
faqs.answer: It is a system that enables the printer to keep track of the remaining length of roll paper. If the system is enabled, the printer automatically prints and reads barcodes on roll paper to accurately estimate the remaining length, and the printer alerts you if the remaining length is not sufficient for the current print job.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the standard printer and the Commercial Edition of my product?
faqs.answer: The Standard Edition uses the standard 11 color ink cartridges. The Commercial Edition uses a Violet (V) cartridge in place of the Light Light Black (LLK) ink cartridge. For this reason, the Commercial Edition is not meant to be used with photo applications.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.
